claims.text: The booked optimal route for TRP-09111 was 12.0 km (trip_record.optimal_distance_km), while the GPS trace of the completed trip measures 16.2 km (gps_trace.trace_distance_km, the governing figure under POL-RD-01). That is an excess of 4.2 km, or 35.0% of optimal. Both establishment gates in POL-RD-01 are passed - the excess is greater than 20% of optimal distance AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms - so the route deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own trace, independently of any profile evidence.

The trace the excess is measured from is clean for POL-RD-07 purposes and for the POL-RD-08 burden: 205 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds. No limb of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) is met, so the trace is not impaired for policy purposes and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises. The rider has therefore discharged the POL-RD-08(a) and (b) burden on the trace alone, and the burden shifts to the driver.

No rider-requested detour can be made out. The chat_log holds exactly two messages: the rider at 08:12 writing 'The navigation route was left after Pioneer Road. Please return to the booked route.' and the driver at 08:12:35 replying 'I am following the road ahead.' Neither message identifies a place or road to divert to, waypoint_hint is null on both, and the rider's message asks for the booked route rather than a detour. The driver's own counterparty_statement likewise claims no stop was requested. POL-RD-04 is unavailable on this record and cannot exculpate any part of the 4.2 km excess.

No road-closure exoneration is available under POL-RD-03. EV-ADVIS-09111-01 is MISSING: it carries the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, status MISSING and weight_multiplier 0.0, so it can carry no fact - but its absence is itself citable, and no traffic advisory covering the booked route and the 2026-09-18 trip window exists. The driver's bare assertion that he 'followed the road available to me' names no advisory ID and no affected segment, and under POL-RD-08 a general assertion unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID does not discharge the driver's burden to point to a specific artifact and clause.

No relocation re-quote changes the baseline. The trip_record shows pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at both null and amended_optimal_distance_km null, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run and the booked optimal of 12.0 km / 24.0 min stands as the comparator for POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, not discretion, and the upfront-quote bar in POL-RD-11 does not apply: the fare_breakdown records fare_model METERED, so this is not a UPFRONT_QUOTE trip and no distance-or-time recovery is closed off.

Running the POL-RD-02 recomputation on the recorded constants: ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 12.0 km + 0.28 x 24.0 min) x 1.2 surge, the multiplier read from fare_breakdown EV-FARE-09111 and from nowhere else) + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 ERP for the only on-optimal-route gantry (Pioneer Road inbound) + 0.00 waiting_time_fee - 1.00 promo_discount = 24.224 recomputed_fare. Charged_total is 33.36, so the refund is 33.36 - 24.224 = 9.136, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 = SGD 9.15. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and far below 90% of charged_total, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 9.15 - exactly the sum the rider contested.

The 2.00 ERP charge for the Tuas South Avenue 8 loop gantry is off-route: the fare_breakdown itself marks that line on_optimal_route false and the nearest trace fix is 1646 m away. Under POL-RD-09(1) that off-route charge is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund, because the recomputed fare admits only gantries lying on the optimal route; it is itemised in the ruling for transparency but must NEVER be added on top of the SGD 9.15. By contrast the Pioneer Road inbound gantry (1.00) is on the optimal route and is properly chargeable, and is the only ERP line carried into the recomputation.

The rider carries no adverse credibility weighting on the profile fields POL-RD-08 names: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the heightened-corroboration override for a claim with excess below 30% is not engaged and the rider's claim needs no source beyond the unimpaired trace. Under POL-GEN-01 no other rider_profile field may ground a finding against the rider.

On the only two counters POL-RD-06 permits, the driver's trailing window is clean: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 610, a rate of 0.00, nowhere near the 0.05 ratio or the 3-flag count the clause requires. Under POL-RD-09(1) the off-route SGD 2.00 is already comprehended in any POL-RD-02 recomputation, because the recomputed fare counts only gantries lying on the optimal route. Any recomputation under POL-RD-02 must be run in full and not in the rider's favour selectively: the base, distance and time components are multiplied by the surge_multiplier of 1.20 recorded on the fare_breakdown, the SGD 0.80 platform fee is added, only the SGD 1.00 on-route ERP is added, and the SGD 1.00 promo discount is deducted. The rider recovers the difference the excess created on those terms, not a re-based fare stripped of surge or platform fee.

An absent artifact carries weight 0.0 and can establish no fact; the case must be decided on the unimpaired trace itself.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: this decides the dispute over trip TRP-09111 (18 September 2026, Pioneer Crescent to Tuas View Square). The rider is partly right; the balance of the metered fare stands.

1) Did the route deviate? Yes, and the trace proves it. Under POL-RD-01 the governing distance is the GPS trace length of 16.2 km (EV-GPS-09111); the 16.2 km on the trip record is a rounded copy of the same measurement and may not be used for the threshold test. The booked optimal is 12.0 km (trip_record.optimal_distance_km). Excess = 4.2 km = 35.0%. Both gates are passed (over 20% and over 0.8 km), so a deviation is ESTABLISHED. The trace is clean for this purpose — 205 fixes at 10-second spacing, 100% coverage, no gaps — so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07, and the rider has carried the POL-RD-08 burden.

2) Is it a MATERIAL deviation? No. 35% is below the 50% mark and 4.2 km is below the 8.0 km mark, so POL-RD-06 is not triggered on materiality. In any event the driver's trailing window is clean (deviation_flags_90d = 0 over completed_trips_90d = 610), so there is no repeat-deviation pattern, no FULL_REFUND uplift, and no driver-conduct referral. The lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is context only under POL-GEN-01 and was not used against either party.

3) Does anything excuse the excess? No. There is no traffic advisory covering this route and window — EV-ADVIS-09111-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) and can carry no fact, though its absence is itself evidence — so POL-RD-03 cannot run, and the driver's statement that he 'followed the road available' cites no advisory ID and does not discharge the driver's burden under POL-RD-08. The chat log (EV-CHAT-09111) holds no rider instruction to detour or to stop, and both waypoint_hint fields are null, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable; the rider in fact asked to return to the booked route. No pickup or dropoff amendment is recorded, so POL-RD-05 does not run. The full 4.2 km excess stands.

4) The refund. The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-11 does not apply and POL-RD-02 fixes the arithmetic. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 12.0 + 0.28 x 24.0) x 1.20 surge, read from EV-FARE-09111 and nowhere else) + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 ERP for the only on-optimal-route gantry (Pioneer Road inbound) - 1.00 promo = 24.224. charged_total = 33.36. Refund = 33.36 - 24.224 = 9.136, rounded UP to SGD 9.15. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and well below 90% of charged_total, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND.

5) The extra ERP charge the rider raised. The SGD 2.00 Tuas South Avenue 8 loop line is not on the optimal route (on_optimal_route false). Under POL-RD-09(1) it is already comprehended in the SGD 9.15 above, because the recomputed fare counts only gantries lying on the optimal route; it is itemised here for transparency and is NOT added on top. The SGD 1.00 Pioneer Road inbound gantry is on the optimal route, is properly chargeable, and is the only ERP carried into the recomputation. No separate ERP refund is due, and no billing-integrity referral arises.

6) Confidence and escalation. The deciding facts rest on the GPS trace, trip record and fare breakdown, each at weight 1.0; the missing advisory carries no deciding fact. Confidence is 0.95, above the 0.70 floor, so the case is not escalated.

Outcome: PARTIAL_REFUND — SGD 9.15 is returned to the rider, the balance of the metered fare stands, and the driver receives no compensation (the meter billed the full 16.2 km the trace records, so there is no unbilled distance).
